problem: MLLM-based VLN agents rely on imitation learning plus DAgger, which needs large expert data and costly retraining. Prior VLN RL methods (VLN-R1, OctoNav) lack dynamic environment interaction and use expert trajectories for reward shaping, so gains over IL are marginal.
motivation: IL suffers from covariate shift, and DAgger only partly fixes it at high data and training cost. Letting the agent explore in the simulator and learn from its own trajectories with a simple outcome reward could give larger gains with little expert supervision.
key_idea: Bootstrap a Qwen2.5-VL-3B agent with IL on a small amount of expert data, then post-train it with multi-turn GRPO in the simulator using a soft success reward, with dynamic early stopping to make rollouts cheap.
insight: The multi-turn formulation is the key enabler: after RL, multi-turn gains +11.6 SR on R2R (38.5 to 50.1) versus only +0.6 for single-turn (39.7 to 40.3), because outcome gradients reach all earlier actions. A simple soft success reward beat hard success and nDTW path-alignment rewards (SR 48.1 vs 46.2 / 44.4-46.3), so imitating the expert path in the reward hurts exploration. Early stopping at 2x the oracle length prunes about 10% of rollouts and cuts rollout time by about 10%.
method: Multi-turn paradigm: actions are generated autoregressively from the instruction, past observations and past actions, which allows KV-cache reuse and lets trajectory-level gradients reach all earlier actions.
Compact action prediction: consecutive same-type actions are merged (e.g. FORWARD 75cm) and the agent predicts action chunks of up to 3 actions per step to shorten episodes.
Stage 1 IL bootstrap: supervised training on 167.6k expert trajectories (R2R, R2R-EnvDrop, RxR), updating the connector and LLM with the vision encoder frozen.
Stage 2 active exploration with GRPO: 8 prompts x 4 rollouts per batch, no KL term, clip 0.28, dynamic sampling (max 2 attempts) to keep at least one success per group, with no expert actions needed.
Soft success reward: R = 15 * I(success) * d_goal/3, where success means STOP within 3 m of the goal.
Dynamic early-stopping: a rollout is terminated and marked failed once its length exceeds 2x the oracle trajectory length.
Engineering: scene caching, scene preloading pipelined with policy updates, and the simulator deployed as a standalone HTTP server for parallel environments.

setting.training_data: IL: 167.6k expert trajectories (10.8k R2R, 146.3k R2R-EnvDrop, 10.5k RxR; about 177K VLN in the RxR table), no extra VQA or web data. RL: 4k instructions each from R2R and RxR, without GT actions.
setting.observation: forward-facing monocular RGB with history of observations and actions
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD / LEFT / RIGHT / STOP with merged actions and chunks of up to 3
setting.privileged: none at test time (the oracle path length and success signal are used only in RL training for early stopping and reward)

numbers.extra: IL on 167.6k expert trajectories + RL on 4k R2R and 4k RxR instructions; RGB only

results: ActiveVLN reaches 50.1 SR / 43.7 SPL on R2R-CE val-unseen and 50.7 SR on RxR-CE with only a 3B model and VLN-only data. RL adds +11.6 SR on R2R and +9.7 on RxR over IL, more than DAgger on its own model (+6.9), StreamVLN (+5.3) and VLN-R1 (+5.3). It is competitive with but slightly below StreamVLN 7B (50.8 SR on R2R, 52.9 on RxR).
limitations: SPL is lower than the strongest baselines (RxR SPL 41.2 vs StreamVLN 46.0) because exploration deviates from expert paths.
RL SR peaks around step 350 then slightly declines, and the single-turn baseline starts higher than the multi-turn one before RL.
Real-world evidence is qualitative only, and reward depends on simulator ground truth (goal distance, oracle path length).
